concept_name: Dynamic Market Curve Arbitrage & Scarcity Trickling
mechanic_exploited: Exploits the asymmetric non-linear price functions (price = base + sign * amp * f(|inv - I0|)) across product types. Staple products (Wheat, Egg) feature logarithmic glut curves ('log'), allowing continuous volume selling without price collapse (e.g. 1,000 eggs yield ~$39,800 at ~$38/unit). Premium products (Melon, Milk, Wool, Strawberry) feature square or linear glut curves that rapidly floor at $1 upon minor oversupply, but feature steep scarcity pricing (up to $266–$334) when market inventory drops below I0 = 10,000 due to guaranteed town demand drain. Exploitation involves continuous dumping of log-curve staples, strict trickling of premium items only during market deficits matching town consumption rates, and front-running single-wave dumps for high-base one-time crops like Melon.
implementation_complexity: Moderate (approx. 50–150 lines of market state evaluation and threshold-based order queueing in python)
expected_yield_gain: +30,000 to +60,000 coins net margin gain (boosting end-game bank to $60,000–$90,000+ vs $10,000–$25,000 baseline)
